{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.4,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R96"],
      "pins": ["R96.1", "R96.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R96 is labelled with value \"24k\" (and simulated as 24k in SPICE), but its MPN (FRC0805J240TSD), its description (\"24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor\") and its footprint/LCSC data all describe a 24 Ω part. The value field and the installed part disagree.",
      "expected": "A 24 kΩ bleed resistor across the VOUTP/VOUTN supply, as the value field states, with a matching 24 kΩ part. A 24 Ω part across a high-voltage output would dissipate far more than a 0805 can handle.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R96\") (value \"24k\") (footprint \"Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R96 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24 Ω part is what was populated, it would load the output heavily, overheat the 0805 resistor and collapse the supply. If the value is the error, the bleed network is not what the schematic intends.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D24", "D25", "D30"],
      "pins": ["D24.2", "D25.2", "D30.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0064"],
      "observed": "The anodes of the three Ethernet status LEDs D24, D25 and D30 share a net (/NET0064) that contains only these three anode pins. Nothing connects it to +3V3, a pull-up, or any driver. Their cathodes go through R19, R58 and R44 to Module2 pins 17, 21 and 15 (Ethernet_nLED2, PI_nLED_Activity, Ethernet_nLED3). Those pins are active-low drive outputs.",
      "expected": "The common anode of these LEDs must return to the 3.3 V rail (as the other status LEDs do, e.g. D40, D41, D22 which take their anodes from +3V3 via R36, R29 or directly). Without that, the active-low CM4 outputs cannot light the LEDs.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"21\") (name \"/NET0064\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D24\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D25\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D30\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Module2\") (pin \"21\") (pinfunction \"PI_nLED_Activity\") (pintype \"open_collector\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"1\") (name \"+3V3\") (class \"Med Power\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "The Ethernet activity/link LEDs and the Pi activity LED never light, because their anodes have no supply path. This removes status indication but does not affect core functions.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist is largely consistent with its SPICE mirror and with a plausible power, USB, CAN and Ethernet design. The two findings are a resistor whose value field (24k) contradicts its installed part data (24 Ω), and a set of LED anodes that have no supply connection; both are moderate-confidence."
}

anomalies.observed: R96 is labelled with value "24k" (and simulated as 24k in SPICE), but its MPN (FRC0805J240TSD), its description ("24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor") and its footprint/LCSC data all describe a 24 Ω part. The value field and the installed part disagree.
anomalies.expected: A 24 kΩ bleed resistor across the VOUTP/VOUTN supply, as the value field states, with a matching 24 kΩ part. A 24 Ω part across a high-voltage output would dissipate far more than a 0805 can handle.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is what was populated, it would load the output heavily, overheat the 0805 resistor and collapse the supply. If the value is the error, the bleed network is not what the schematic intends.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three Ethernet status LEDs D24, D25 and D30 share a net (/NET0064) that contains only these three anode pins. Nothing connects it to +3V3, a pull-up, or any driver. Their cathodes go through R19, R58 and R44 to Module2 pins 17, 21 and 15 (Ethernet_nLED2, PI_nLED_Activity, Ethernet_nLED3). Those pins are active-low drive outputs.
anomalies.expected: The common anode of these LEDs must return to the 3.3 V rail (as the other status LEDs do, e.g. D40, D41, D22 which take their anodes from +3V3 via R36, R29 or directly). Without that, the active-low CM4 outputs cannot light the LEDs.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity/link LEDs and the Pi activity LED never light, because their anodes have no supply path. This removes status indication but does not affect core functions.
